scenes.tts: In December 1964, an expedition worked on Rapa Nui. One member, Georges Nogrady, collected soil. In Montreal, a bacterium was found to kill fungi. In 1972, Suren Sehgal isolated the compound and named it rapamycin. But why does it also stop cells from growing?
scenes.visual: Island blob with a soil chip travels to a Montreal chip; a bacterium chip kills a fungus chip; 1972 flask yields a rapamycin chip; a question mark appears over a growing cell.

scenes.tts: In Michael Hall's laboratory, Joseph Heitman spread yeast on plates containing rapamycin, and kept the rare mutants that grew anyway. Most had mutations in the gene for F P R one, the yeast version of F K B P twelve. So rapamycin does nothing alone. It must first bind F K B P twelve. The pair is the poison.
scenes.visual: A plate full of yeast dots with rapamycin: nearly all fade, a few stay and are kept; most of the kept ones are tagged with the FPR1 gene chip (yeast FKBP12); then rapamycin alone does nothing, binds FKBP12, and the pair turns red.

scenes.tts: The remaining mutants had changes in one of two new genes, T O R one and T O R two, for target of rapamycin. The screen was published in 1991. In 1994 and 1995, several laboratories found the mammalian protein the pair binds. Its name is m-TOR.
scenes.visual: The remaining mutants split into two gene chips TOR1 and TOR2 with 'target of rapamycin'; a timeline gets 1991 then 1994 to 1995; the FKBP12-rapamycin pair docks onto a mammalian protein that is named mTOR.

scenes.tts: m-TOR is a large kinase. Beside its kinase domain is a small domain called F R B. Rapamycin sits between F K B P twelve and F R B like glue between two blocks. The bound F K B P twelve narrows the substrates' path to the active site. The drug does not compete with A T P. It is allosteric: it acts from a site other than the active site.
scenes.visual: Schematic mTOR with kinase domain and a small FRB domain; FKBP12 and rapamycin glue on beside FRB; the substrate path to the active site narrows; a crossed-out compete-with-ATP chip; active site and drug site are marked as two different places.
scenes.caption: mTOR is a large kinase. Beside its kinase domain is a small domain called FRB. Rapamycin sits between FKBP12 and FRB like glue between two blocks. The bound FKBP12 narrows the substrates' path to the active site. The drug does not compete with ATP. It is allosteric: it acts from a site other than the active site.
